- Practised making 100 with tens numbers, including 30 + 70 and 80 + 20; some answers were right, but the method was not steady yet.
- Practised 1-jumps and 10-jumps on a number line; the number of jumps to 100 still needs checking next time.

end.parentNote: Vihaan practised making 100 with tens, using 1- and 10-jumps, and finding the partner for 65. They used tens language well for examples such as 30 + 70 and 80 + 20, and they noticed that 65 + 45 makes 110. The 45/35 mix-up was not corrected at the last check, so this needs more practice. At home, use ten-rupee groups and ask, “How many more to make 100?” then check by adding both numbers.
